title: “All the corn was frozen. The little leaves were stiff, and broke if ...
description: “All the corn was frozen. The little leaves were stiff, and broke if you touched them. Only cold water would save the life of the corn. Every hill must be watered before the sunshine touched it, or that plant would die.” Can you imagine them watering three acres of corn with buckets by hand when their livelihood depended on it?  Our gardens were hit with a freeze a couple nights ago when temps dipped lower than they were supposed to, and our peas and Romanesco froze solid. We never plant our anything that’s not cold hardy before last frost, but these guys can take some cold so out they go! They still don’t like to freeze hard, though. I’ve used this trick a few times in the garden, and while there are times it won’t work, there are many times it’s saved my plants! The theory is that the damage in frosted plants comes from the expansion of the water within the cells, and that damage is exacerbated by rapid temperature changes, like when the sun hits a frozen plant. Therefore, by watering with COLD water before the sun has a chance to hit, the plant is slowly warmed, reducing damage. Big growers do this with large overhead sprinklers that they run throughout the night, but this isn’t really feasible for most home gardeners, so this is something to try! Have you ever done this? Did it work, or not? #garden #frost #frozengarden #flowergarden #gardenersworld #gardentok #gardeningtiktok #gardenhacks #growyourown #homesteading
